AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why do we sprinkle soil or old compost between layers? (1 mark)
   A. It adds plastic
   B. It makes the heap sweeter
   C. It keeps birds away
   D. It adds tiny living things that help wastes to rot

2. Which of these is a brown material for a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Fresh cow dung
   B. Dry leaves
   C. Vegetable peelings
   D. Fresh weeds

3. Why is a compost heap turned with a fork? (1 mark)
   A. To add plastic
   B. To remove all the water
   C. To make it smaller
   D. To let in air and mix the materials

4. How can compost be used in a garden? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it away
   B. Mix it in planting holes or spread it around crops
   C. Use it to build a wall
   D. Feed it to fish

5. Why should the drip container be covered? (1 mark)
   A. To increase evaporation
   B. To warm the water
   C. To keep out leaves and mosquitoes
   D. To make water sweet

6. What does mulch do? (1 mark)
   A. Kills the plant
   B. Keeps the soil moist by reducing evaporation
   C. Makes the soil hot
   D. Adds plastic to the soil

7. Why should the holes in a drip pipe be tiny? (1 mark)
   A. So the water is warm
   B. So water drips slowly
   C. So the pipe becomes lighter
   D. So water pours out fast

8. What could a school use to make a simple drip system? (1 mark)
   A. A plastic bottle with tiny holes in the cap
   B. A broom
   C. A wooden door
   D. A stone

9. Which is a problem of cutting many trees for firewood? (1 mark)
   A. The soil becomes richer
   B. More rain falls at once
   C. Trees grow faster
   D. Forests shrink and soil can be washed away

10. What does it mean to conserve fuel? (1 mark)
   A. To burn as much as possible
   B. To use only what is needed and make it last
   C. To waste it
   D. To hide it

11. What should you do after the water starts to boil? (1 mark)
   A. Add paraffin
   B. Turn the flame down or move wood back
   C. Add more wood
   D. Open the pot and blow on it

12. Which is a benefit of using less fuel? (1 mark)
   A. The family spends more
   B. The family saves money
   C. More smoke is made
   D. More trees must be cut

13. Why should a scarecrow be moved every few days? (1 mark)
   A. It gets too hot
   B. The pole is too heavy
   C. Animals get used to one that never moves
   D. It grows

14. Which of these is a peaceful way of protecting fruit from birds? (1 mark)
   A. Burning the trees
   B. Covering trees with a light net
   C. Setting traps that kill
   D. Poisoning the birds

15. Why is poison a bad way to deal with wild animals? (1 mark)
   A. It is too cheap
   B. It is too slow to spread
   C. It can also kill other animals and people
   D. It makes crops grow

16. Why are tins with pebbles tied on a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. They store water
   B. They make noise and flash to frighten animals
   C. They feed birds
   D. They make it heavy

17. Why do crowded seedlings grow badly? (1 mark)
   A. They get too much space
   B. They like company
   C. They have no roots
   D. They compete for water, light and food

18. What should be done first before pulling out seedlings when thinning? (1 mark)
   A. Dry the bed
   B. Water the bed so the soil is soft
   C. Cover it with plastic
   D. Cut the tops off

19. How can a person without a garden grow tiny-seeded crops? (1 mark)
   A. Only in a forest
   B. On hard rock
   C. On a road
   D. In a container seedbed with drainage holes

20. Which crop is established by direct sowing of tiny seeds? (1 mark)
   A. Carrot
   B. Banana
   C. Mango
   D. Sweet potato

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. List three materials that can be used to make a scarecrow. (3 marks)

22. Name two things that should never be put in a compost heap and say why. (2 marks)

23. A school wants to make compost from kitchen and garden wastes. Write a plan with the materials, the place, the steps and the safety measures. (5 marks)

24. Give three benefits of using compost manure on the farm. (3 marks)

25. Name three crops established by direct sowing of tiny seeds. (3 marks)

26. List three things needed to make a bucket drip system. (3 marks)

27. Give three ways of saving fuel when cooking. (3 marks)

28. Describe how to prepare a fine seedbed in three steps. (3 marks)

29. Explain why drip irrigation is useful in a dry area and describe how a school could set up a system for a row of kale. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — It adds tiny living things that help wastes to rot
   Soil and old compost carry bacteria and fungi that break down wastes.

2. B — Dry leaves
   Brown materials are dry, like dry leaves, dry grass and straw.

3. D — To let in air and mix the materials
   Mixing brings outer material to the middle so all rots evenly.

4. B — Mix it in planting holes or spread it around crops
   Compost feeds crops and improves the soil.

5. C — To keep out leaves and mosquitoes
   A cover keeps water clean and stops mosquitoes breeding.

6. B — Keeps the soil moist by reducing evaporation
   A covering of dry grass slows down drying of the soil.

7. B — So water drips slowly
   Small holes give slow drips that soak into the soil.

8. A — A plastic bottle with tiny holes in the cap
   A bottle with small holes in its cap drips slowly.

9. D — Forests shrink and soil can be washed away
   Trees protect soil and water, so cutting them harms the environment.

10. B — To use only what is needed and make it last
   Conserving fuel means saving it.

11. B — Turn the flame down or move wood back
   A gentle flame is enough to keep the water boiling.

12. B — The family saves money
   Buying less fuel means spending less.

13. C — Animals get used to one that never moves
   Animals learn that something still is harmless.

14. B — Covering trees with a light net
   A net keeps birds away without harming them.

15. C — It can also kill other animals and people
   Poison harms living things that are not the target.

16. B — They make noise and flash to frighten animals
   Noise and movement scare animals.

17. D — They compete for water, light and food
   Too many plants in a small space fight for resources.

18. B — Water the bed so the soil is soft
   Wet soil lets you pull gently without harming others.

19. D — In a container seedbed with drainage holes
   A box or tin with holes and fine soil works well.

20. A — Carrot
   Carrots are sown directly because transplanting damages their roots.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sticks or poles, old clothes, a sack, dry grass, string, tins, old CDs (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct material.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Plastic and glass, because they do not rot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two items, 1 mark for the reason.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: Materials: peelings, leaves, grass. Place: shaded, well-drained, near the garden. Steps: sticks, layers, water, cover, turn. Safety: gloves, wash hands, keep children away from the heap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 for place, 2 for steps, 1 for safety.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: It feeds crops, it softens the soil and helps it to hold water, and it is cheap because it uses waste.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct benefit.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Carrot, millet, amaranth, radish, sorghum (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each crop.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: A bucket or container, a hose or pipe, and small holes or drippers for water to come out. A stand may also be used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a lid on the pot, cut food small, use dry firewood, put out the fire after cooking, soak beans first, or use an improved jiko (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear weeds and stones; dig and loosen the soil; break the lumps with a rake until fine and level (add compost).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

29. (5 marks)
   Answer: It saves scarce water because water reaches roots directly and little is lost. For kale: raise a bucket on a stand, attach a hose along the row, close the end, ask an adult to make small holes beside each plant, fill with clean water and check that drips are slow.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons, 3 marks for set-up steps.
